name: Netherlands
tagline: A country built on purpose, mostly below sea level, and cycled end to end.
summary: A quarter of the Netherlands lies below sea level and nearly all of it was arranged by people — drained, diked, pumped and planned. That habit of design runs through the painting, the cities and the bicycle infrastructure, which is the best on earth and not close. Amsterdam absorbs most visitors; Utrecht, Rotterdam and the northern islands absorb almost none.

season.note: The bulb fields flower from late March to mid-May and that is a genuine spectacle with genuine crowds. Summer is long-evening terrace weather. Winter is grey and flat, and the museums are empty, which is a fair trade.

getting_around: Trains are frequent and the whole country is inside two hours. Rent a bicycle in every city; the lanes are separated, signposted and used by everyone from toddlers to pensioners in suits. The OV-chipkaart or a contactless card covers everything.
food: Raw herring, held by the tail, with onion — in season from June
Stroopwafel, made fresh on a market griddle rather than boxed
Indonesian rijsttafel, a colonial legacy taken very seriously

festivals.name: King's Day — the whole country in orange, and a national flea market

know: Do not walk in the bicycle lane. This is the single most reliable way to annoy a Dutch person.
Amsterdam's centre is heavily regulated now — tours, rentals and behaviour all more restricted than the reputation suggests.
Almost everyone speaks excellent English and will switch before you finish your first Dutch sentence.

regions.name: The Randstad
regions.summary: The dense western ring: Amsterdam, Rotterdam, The Hague, Utrecht and the polder between them.

cities.name: Amsterdam
cities.summary: A 17th-century canal plan that still works, with two of the world's great collections inside it.
highlights: The Rijksmuseum, and half an hour in front of the Vermeers
The Van Gogh Museum, booked ahead or not at all
The Jordaan and the Nine Streets on foot
A canal at seven in the morning, before the boats

experiences.name: The city the way it is used
experiences.summary: Rent for a day, ride out to Amsterdam-Noord on the free ferry, and stop thinking of the bicycle as an activity.

cities.name: Rotterdam
cities.summary: Flattened in 1940 and rebuilt as an argument for modern architecture, on Europe's largest port.
highlights: The Markthal, a food market inside a housing block
Depot Boijmans, the first publicly accessible art storage building anywhere
Harbour tours through a port that runs for forty kilometres

cities.name: Utrecht
cities.summary: Amsterdam's canals at half the scale and a fifth of the crowd, with wharf cellars at water level.
highlights: The Oudegracht's two-level canals, unique in Europe
Rietveld's Schröder House, the built manifesto of De Stijl

regions.name: The North & the Wadden Islands
regions.summary: Frisian country, mudflats that appear at low tide, and islands with no cars.

cities.name: Texel
cities.summary: The largest Wadden island: dunes, sheep, seals and thirty kilometres of empty North Sea beach.
highlights: Seal colonies on the sandbanks, seen from a boat
Bird reserves on the migration route, best in spring
Local lamb and a brewery, on an island you can cycle around in a day

experiences.name: Wadlopen — walking the sea floor
experiences.summary: Guided walks across the exposed seabed at low tide, thigh-deep in mud, timed against a returning sea. Never attempted alone.
